reading: Day 3 is verse. Juniper reads a four-line verse about her face-down clock at South House at c49, and the town answers in kind: Birch prints a knot verse learned from Cedar (post 14, c51), Juniper prints the clock (post 15), Alder a verse about folding his map «without choosing a road» (post 16), Iris lines about «room beside someone» (post 17); Cedar keeps one unprinted. Each verse is about the citizen's own item — day 2's noticing, put into four lines. Beside it: a slow round at the square (Cedar's knee rhythm, Dune's words, Elm's flute, c55–58) and at the market Gale's sound-word game, which became a breakfast story of a toast-bearer who counts cups, told by nine (c56–63). The travel record of day 2 is named three times. Verses: 10 citizens, 125 entries; the word game and its story: 9 citizens, 60 entries. No proposals, no rules, no exits.
